best_for: Animators and small studios who scan paper drawings and want a free xsheet-based production tool with Studio Ghibli roots, and who can live without a polished Mac or Linux setup.

points.title: Built from Studio Ghibli's Toonz
points.text: OpenToonz comes from Toonz, which Studio Ghibli customized and used for ink and paint, color design and compositing on nearly all its films. Dwango opened it up with Digital Video and Ghibli, so you get a tool shaped by real feature production.

points.title: Free for studio work
points.text: Most of the code is under the Modified BSD license, and the project says you can use and change it for business or personal work at no cost. The installer has its own terms of use, so read them if you plan to redistribute it.

points.title: Paper scanning is a core job
points.text: The GTS tool, written by Ghibli, scans numbered drawing sequences with saved settings from a TWAIN scanner. GTS runs only on Windows, so a Mac or Linux setup loses that part of the pipeline.

points.title: Xsheet, timeline and effect nodes
points.text: You can time shots in an xsheet or a timeline, build effects in a node tree, and work with raster and vector drawings in the same scene. A plug-in SDK lets developers add their own image effects.

points.title: Check the system floor
points.text: The official page lists 64-bit Windows 7 SP1, 8.1 or 10, and macOS 10.14 Mojave or later, with 4 GB of RAM recommended. Some manuals exist only in Japanese, and English help comes mostly from a user group.

points.title: Mac and Linux builds have catches
points.text: Homebrew disabled its OpenToonz cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Apple's Gatekeeper check, so expect a security prompt on first launch. The Linux Flatpak here is x64 only and is not marked as verified by Flathub.

points.title: Few versions to roll back to
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 2 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current 1.8.0, so older builds there mean the project's GitHub releases page.
